objective: GitLab job-token allowlist vs package-registry endpoints

observations.text: code: lib/api/pypi_packages.rb, composer_packages.rb, npm_namespace_endpoints.rb accept job tokens without allowlist check; container registry routes carry job_token_scope: :project; GraphQL rejects job tokens outright

assumptions.believes: a job token can only reach its allowlisted projects
assumptions.violated_if: PyPI/Composer/npm routes serve packages outside the allowlist

assumptions.believes: skip_job_token_policies is only an auth convenience flag
assumptions.violated_if: the flag silently drops scope enforcement too

hypotheses.statement: Same object (Package, Project, JobToken) is reachable through a different verb, endpoint, or content-type that skips the enforcement at 'authorize_job_token_policies! in lib/api/helpers.rb'.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Violate the assumption by leaving the guarded channel and entering an unguarded one.
hypotheses.defender_view: The alternate channel may enforce the same rule at a different layer, or the object may not exist there.
hypotheses.devil_view: The 'alternate channel' might require stronger auth, making this a downgrade that never reaches the check.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Fire the same logical action through GET vs POST vs PUT vs PATCH vs a versioned path; compare outcomes.
hypotheses.killed_by: All channels enforce the check identically.

hypotheses.statement: A value written in one feature is consumed/rendered in another without re-running the validation done at 'authorize_job_token_policies! in lib/api/helpers.rb'.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Write where validation is weak, execute where trust is high (stored XSS, formula injection, template render).
hypotheses.defender_view: The consuming feature may sanitize on render; writing is not exploiting.
hypotheses.devil_view: The two features may share the same validation pipeline, so nothing is skipped.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Write a probe payload in the weakest input, then observe every surface that renders it (list, export, notification, API).

hypotheses.statement: Upstream validates at 'authorize_job_token_policies! in lib/api/helpers.rb', but a downstream component across a trust boundary (runner->API, API->database) trusts the value under different rules.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Find where validation and consumption disagree (client-side vs server-side, API vs webhook, SSO claim vs local session).
hypotheses.defender_view: Defense in depth may re-validate downstream; one layer's trust is not the system's trust.
hypotheses.devil_view: The boundary may carry a signed/verified token, so downstream trust is justified.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Tamper the value at the boundary (proxy match/replace) and watch whether downstream re-validates.

hypotheses.statement: An identifier is normalized differently by the layer that checks 'authorize_job_token_policies! in lib/api/helpers.rb' and the layer that uses it (case, encoding, numeric-vs-string, trailing slash, unicode).
hypotheses.attacker_view: Supply two spellings of the same identity: one that passes the check, one that resolves to the target.
hypotheses.defender_view: Canonicalization may happen before the check, collapsing both spellings to the same value.
hypotheses.devil_view: The identifier may be an opaque UUID where normalization is a no-op.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Send case/encoding/whitespace variants of a known-good and a known-bad identifier; compare accept/reject matrices.

hypotheses.statement: A state transition (JobToken: issued -> scoped -> used) leaves stale state: the system believes the old state, another layer believes the new one.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Act on the object in the window where two layers disagree (scheduled publish to a deleted board, cached public copy of a re-secreted object).
hypotheses.defender_view: Caches and schedules are eventually consistent; a brief stale window is not a vulnerability.
hypotheses.devil_view: The transition may be atomic across layers, so no window exists.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Force the transition, then immediately probe every layer (API, unauthenticated cache, export, search index).
hypotheses.killed_by: All layers agree within the probe window.

hypotheses.statement: Client-visible arithmetic (credits, quotas, counts) can be desynced from the server's bookkeeping that 'authorize_job_token_policies! in lib/api/helpers.rb' relies on.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Drive the counter through lifecycle events (create/delete empty objects, retries, back-button resubmits) and watch for drift.
hypotheses.defender_view: Counters are server-computed; the client display is cosmetic.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Cycle the lifecycle event repeatedly and compare the counter before/after against the expected delta.
hypotheses.killed_by: The counter always matches the expected arithmetic.
